items.title: FusionGDB 3.0: integrating breakpoints, generating personalized sequences, and inferring tumorigenic scenarios for human fusion genes.
items.summary: Journal: Nucleic acids research. Abstract: FusionGDB has served diverse biological, health, and clinical research communities as a unique functional annotation knowledgebase of human fusion genes. In this study, we report an updated resource of human fusion gene annotation (FusionGDB 3.0), available at https://compbio.uth.edu/FusionGDB/. FusionGDB 3.0 includes substantial content updates: 156K up-to-date human fusion genes established by integrating 216K RNA-seq-based and 100K WGS-based breakpoint events, comprehensive open reading frame annotations, protein domain retention searches, and 1.13 million personalized fusion protein sequences reflecting individual nsSNVs from TCGA and CCLE, as well as N- and C-truncated protein sequences alongside canonical in-frame products. Furthermore, it incorporates 18K potential tumorigenic scenarios, supported by evidence from the literature, spanning drug-targetable gene group fusions, the epigenomic architecture around breakpoint junctions, and therapeutic prioritization scoring. FusionGDB 3.0 establishes a systematic framework for the functional annotation of coding structural variants. FusionGDB 3.0 serves as a pivotal reference knowledgebase for the genomics, oncology, and precision pharmacology communities, while also functioning as a foundational benchmark dataset for training and validating machine learning models, structural biology platforms, and AI-driven therapeutic discovery pipelines.
items.headline: FusionGDB 3.0: Comprehensive Functional Annotation of Human Fusion Genes
items.brief: FusionGDB 3.0 integrates 156K human fusion genes from RNA-seq and WGS breakpoint data, annotating open reading frames, protein domain retention, and personalized fusion protein sequences reflecting individual variants. It includes 18K tumorigenic scenarios with epigenomic context and therapeutic prioritization, providing a systematic framework for functional interpretation of fusion genes in cancer.
items.why: This resource advances computational genomics by enabling detailed functional and personalized analysis of fusion genes, crucial for understanding cancer biology and guiding precision medicine.
items.korean: FusionGDB 3.0은 인간 융합 유전자의 기능적 주석과 개인 맞춤형 단백질 서열을 통합하여 암 연구에 중요한 도구를 제공합니다.

items.title: Lysine-specific demethylase 1 links metabolism to stemness in human neural stem cells.
items.summary: Journal: Stem cell reports. Abstract: Epigenetic regulation of stem cell fate requires tight coordination with cellular metabolism; however, key downstream effectors remain poorly defined. Here, we show that lysine-specific demethylase 1 (LSD1) governs metabolic programs essential for stemness in human fetal neural stem cells. LSD1 inhibition induced a pronounced glycolytic shift accompanied by altered lineage commitment, characterized by suppression of neuronal differentiation and promotion of astrocytic fate. Machine learning-based Elastic Net analysis of transcriptomic data identified a subset of metabolic genes, including PLPP2 and CPT1A, which regulate phospholipid metabolism and mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation, as key downstream effectors of LSD1. Functional perturbation experiments showed that knockdown of these candidates attenuated LSD1 inhibition-induced glycolytic activation and ameliorated distinct differentiation phenotypes. Chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing revealed LSD1 occupancy at metabolic gene loci, supporting their transcriptional repression by LSD1. Together, these findings identify LSD1 as an epigenetic gatekeeper preserving stemness by restraining glycolysis and inappropriate lineage commitment.
items.headline: LSD1 Links Metabolism to Stemness in Human Neural Stem Cells
items.brief: Lysine-specific demethylase 1 (LSD1) regulates metabolic programs essential for stemness in human fetal neural stem cells. LSD1 inhibition shifts metabolism towards glycolysis and alters lineage commitment, suppressing neuronal differentiation and promoting astrocytic fate. Machine learning identified metabolic genes regulated by LSD1, and chromatin immunoprecipitation confirmed LSD1 occupancy at these loci, linking epigenetic regulation to metabolic control of stem cell fate.
items.why: This study reveals a mechanistic link between epigenetic regulation and metabolism in neural stem cells, highlighting LSD1 as a key factor integrating chromatin state and metabolic pathways relevant to stemness and differentiation.
items.korean: LSD1은 인간 신경줄기세포에서 대사와 줄기성 유지 조절을 연결하는 핵심 인자임을 보여줍니다.

items.title: Decoding the regulatory programs governing glioblastoma plasticity.
items.summary: Journal: Nature. Abstract: Glioblastoma is incurable and resistant to therapy despite genomic stability under treatment1-8, suggesting that non-genetic cellular plasticity is a central driver of progression. Whether such plasticity reflects stochastic state switching or is governed by predictable gene regulation has remained unclear9-13. Here we introduce scDORI (single-cell deep multi-omic regulatory inference)-a deep-learning framework that infers enhancer-driven gene-regulatory networks at single-cell resolution-and apply it to single-nucleus multiome profiles of more than one million cells from primary glioblastomas. Integrating computational inference with systematic perturbation screens across patient-derived models, we show that a structured regulatory program with an asymmetric interplay of activators and repressors governs cellular plasticity in glioblastoma. The resulting transition landscape is hierarchical and predictable, but permits cross-lineage trajectories that are absent from normal neurodevelopment. Within this landscape, low-plasticity states such as the neuronal-like state are not stable differentiation end points but actively maintained configurations, stabilized by a network of safeguard repressors that silence alternative fates. We identify MYT1L as the dominant member of this network, and show that it binds to and represses master regulators of every alternative state to consolidate neuronal-like identity. MYT1L restricted plasticity even under standard-of-care therapy and suppressed tumour growth and invasion in vivo. Conversely, loss of MYT1L reactivated plasticity and accelerated malignant features, indicating that low-plasticity identity requires continuous repression. These findings reframe malignant cell state stability as a balance between activation and continuous repression, and nominate safeguard repressors as candidate therapeutic targets that are distinct from differentiation-inducing activators, with potential relevance across cancers in which phenotypic switching drives therapy resistance.
items.headline: scDORI: Deep Multi-omic Regulatory Inference Decodes Glioblastoma Plasticity
items.brief: scDORI is a deep-learning framework that infers enhancer-driven gene regulatory networks at single-cell resolution from multiome data. Applied to over one million glioblastoma cells, it reveals a hierarchical and predictable regulatory landscape governing cellular plasticity, with asymmetric activator and repressor interplay. Perturbation screens validate key regulators, showing cross-lineage trajectories absent in normal neurodevelopment, advancing understanding of glioblastoma progression.
items.why: This work provides a novel computational method to dissect gene regulatory programs driving cancer cell plasticity at single-cell multi-omic resolution, enabling mechanistic insights into glioblastoma heterogeneity and progression.
items.korean: scDORI는 단일세포 다중오믹스 데이터를 활용해 교모세포종의 세포 가소성을 조절하는 유전자 네트워크를 해독합니다.
